decisions.reason: As an incremental rye bread in a growing market, it likely meets a modest aspiration level well enough that management has little reason to discontinue it absent clear signs of weak demand.
The award-winning premium raisin stollen is a stated flagship and clearly performs above aspiration, so a German bakery of this type would very likely retain it.

This seeded rye mixed bread fits existing capabilities and customer tastes, and without evidence of failure the firm is likely to keep it while monitoring whether it earns a stable place in the assortment.
Although it faces some risk from overlap with several other new rye breads, it is still close to the established offer and can be carried unless results clearly fall short of aspiration.
A marzipan stollen is closely related to the firm's proven seasonal confectionery strengths, so management is likely to view it as worth keeping unless the season disappoints markedly.
The ancient grain bread adds differentiation but still relies on familiar breadmaking know-how, making retention likely while the firm learns whether the new variant attracts enough demand.
